title: ci(test-shards): refresh the Test Core dataset and cut the CLI into 4 slices on plain-sum placement, and pin the whole-package leg
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DLXndrnCtL5skV6kUMFJ24w)_

Part of #25870. The card stays open until its after-landing reading: the first 10 full merge-queue Test Core builds with no load-shaped red.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What

This is the second attempt at #25870, after #25968 was reverted by #26077. It keeps only the parts of #25968 that did not cause the merge-queue reds. Two files change.

- **`scripts/test-shard-timings.json`**: the 2026-10-26 refresh (14 runs, newest 40272142430). The file is byte-identical to the one #25968 carried (`git diff f36f6190 HEAD -- scripts/test-shard-timings.json` is empty).
- **`scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs`**:
  - `FILE_SHARDED_PACKAGES` cli 3 → 4, and `PREVIOUS_FILE_SHARDED_PACKAGES` = `{cli: 3}`, so the refresh lane can still decode the 3-slice summaries it retains. The derivation table for 4 sits next to the map.
  - **Placement does not change.** `partition()` stays the plain-sum LPT. There is no wall model and no `loadOf`/`wallOf`.
  - **New pin 3d** in `--self-test` (`WHOLE_LEG_CAP_SECONDS`, `LOAD_SENSITIVE_APART`, `wholeLegProblems()`), described below.

No `.github/**` edit, so this is not Tier H, and no governed path is touched.

## Why

- **cli ×4 has to be on `main` before the 2026-11-02 05:30Z weekly refresh.** With the 10-26 weights, pin 3c refuses cli ×3: one slice is 899.15 s, which is past 1.3 × `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`'s 670.12 s = 871.16 s ("Raise it to 4"). If this does not land first, the refresh bot's PR goes red.
- **#25968 failed because of its placement.** The weights and the slice count were not the problem. The wall model moved the whole packages off the slice shards, which left four shards with ~2141 s of four-wide work each, and put objectql and plugin-security on the same shard. Full queue builds then went red 5 times in 27, every time on a load-sensitive test (#26074, and the post-mortem on #25870, comment 6414712442). Keeping plain-sum placement with the refreshed weights makes every whole-package shard *lighter* than it is on main today.

## Shard table: `planRun()` on the full list

These numbers come from `turbo ls --output=json` at 365fe5ec with `--exclude @objectstack/dogfood`, run through `planRun()` exactly as ci.yml calls it. "whole" is the shard's whole-package seconds with the package count in brackets. "slice" is the CLI slice's seconds. "step" is the #25376 wall model (`whole / 2.9 + slice`), included for reference only.

| shard | main (plain sum, 10-23 dataset, cli ×3) | this PR (plain sum, 10-26 dataset, cli ×4) |
|---|---|---|
| 1/8 | 1866 (6) · step 643 | 1499 (16) · step 517 |
| 2/8 | 1866 (11) **objectql** · 643 | 1501 (10) · 518 |
| 3/8 | 900 (8) + cli 1/3 966 · 1276 | 826 (9) + cli 1/4 674 · 959 |
| 4/8 | 900 (9) + cli 2/3 966 · 1276 | 827 (9) + cli 2/4 674 · 959 |
| 5/8 | 899 (8) + cli 3/3 966 **plugin-security** · 1276 | 826 (9) + cli 3/4 674 · 959 |
| 6/8 | 1866 (10) · 643 | 826 (9) + cli 4/4 674 **plugin-security** · 959 |
| 7/8 | 1868 (11) · 644 | 1501 (10) **objectql** · 518 |
| 8/8 | 1866 (19) · 643 | 1500 (10) · 517 |

The dispatch set three conditions, and all three hold:

- Every whole-package shard is at or below today's ~1866 s. The heaviest is 1501 s, against 1868 s on main.
- **objectql (7/8) and plugin-security (6/8) are on different shards.** plugin-security sits on a slice shard with 826 s of whole-package work, as it did before #25968 (899 s).
- No shard's whole sum is above the pre-#25968 mean of 1866 s.

Bin totals are 1499–1501 s (max/mean 1.00×), inside the 2697.45 s density cap. #25968's layout for comparison: 186/185/185/185 + 674 s slices, and 2141/2139/2141/2142 s whole.

## Pin 3d: the whole-package leg cap and the load-sensitive pair

Pins 2–3c grade bin *sums* and slice counts, and #25968's 2141 s layout passed all of them. Pin 3d grades what actually broke, on the committed dataset's full list as CI splits it:

- **`WHOLE_LEG_CAP_SECONDS = 1868`**: no shard's whole-package sum (slices excluded) may exceed 1868 s. That figure is the heaviest whole leg the queue has run green: shard 7/8 of the plain-sum layout on the 2026-10-23 dataset, red 0 times in 19 full builds before #25968 and 0 in 10 after #26077. 2141 s is the figure that went red. The pin's comment says that raising the cap needs a merge-queue red-rate reading, not a balance figure, and that the remedy for a refresh that outgrows the cap is a wider matrix or a finer slice.
- **`LOAD_SENSITIVE_APART = [objectql, plugin-security]`**: these two may never be whole on the same shard. They are the two packages whose tests went red under load in #26074. The third red was a CLI slice, and a slice runs alone after its shard's whole leg. If either package disappears from the split, the pin goes red instead of passing on a pair it no longer grades.

The battery has 5 cases: the committed-dataset grade, which first proves the split's whole-leg sums add up to the dataset's whole seconds, and 4 fixtures (pass, pair together, over cap, member missing). The battery roster floor goes from 15 to 16.

## Tests

- `node scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs --self-test` at HEAD: `self-test OK (75 measured packages -> 78 shard items, 8 shards, max/mean 1.00x <= 1.3x, floor 1169s, bins 1499.31/1501.21/1499.98/1500.86/1499.98/1500.12/1501.22/1500.45s within the 2697.45s density cap, whole legs 1499/1501/826/827/826/826/1501/1500s within 1868s, file-level slices: @objectstack/cli x4)`.
- **Ablation: the pin catches #25968's placement.** I put #25968's load-based `partition()` (slice × 2.9) back in temporarily and turned off pin 2, which on main already reds it at 1.43×. Pin 3d then reds with `shard 5/8 carries 2141s … 6/8 2139s … 7/8 2141s … 8/8 2142s of whole packages, past the 1868s cap` and `@objectstack/objectql and @objectstack/plugin-security share shard 7/8`. That is #25968's layout reproduced. After the ablation the file was restored and `cmp` confirms it matches.
- **Ablation: cli ×3 on the refreshed dataset reds pin 3c** with `sliced 3 ways at 2697.45s, one slice is 899s … Raise it to 4.` Restored afterwards, `cmp` clean.
- Sibling self-tests are green: `measure-test-shard-timings` (decodes through both maps), `check-test-completeness`, `ci/select-shard-timings-run`, `ci/select-shard-packages.selftest.sh` (32 cases).

## Gates

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (merge base 365fe5ec): all 35 derived families exit 0. `dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` reconciles: 35 derived, 35 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
- Serial check before pushing: none of the 36 other open PRs on this repo touches `scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs` or `scripts/test-shard-timings.json`. I checked each with `git diff --name-only origin/main...pull/N/head`.
- Everything else is left to this PR's CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **After landing (the reading #25870 waits on):** read the first 10 full Test Core `merge_group` builds the way #26074's 13:35Z reading did. Any load-shaped red means stop and report, and a revert is on the table. Also: the slowest spec-touching `pull_request` shard on 3 readings, for information. The original goal was ≤ ~20 min. The predicted slice-shard step falls from 1276 s to 959 s, but the cold DTS closure (~5.8 min) still comes on top of that.
- **Left alone because it is Tier H:** ci.yml's Test Core comments still say "3 slices" (the drift-step comment and the timeout history). Correcting them would make this PR Tier H. They are for whichever step edits ci.yml next.
- The pin grades the dataset's full list, which is what a full queue build runs. A `pull_request` or partial `merge_group` run splits its own smaller list, which can put the two packages together on lighter shards. That was already true on the green layout, so this PR does not change it.
